observations: For the post-separation Honeywell Technologies perimeter excluding Aerospace, Q2 2026 sales were $5.187B, up 3% reported and 4% organic year over year.
Honeywell Technologies operating income was $662M, down 1%, with operating margin 12.8% versus 13.3%; segment profit was $985M, up 9%, and segment margin expanded 100 bps to 19.0%.
Honeywell Technologies cash flow from operations was $563M versus $187M and free cash flow was $456M versus $114M in Q2 2025.
Building Automation organic sales grew 9%, segment margin expanded 90 bps to 27.1%, and orders increased 13% led by data-center and hospitality verticals.
Process Automation and Technology organic sales declined 1% and segment margin contracted 180 bps to 22.1%, creating a mixed operating picture inside the post-spin portfolio.
Industrial Automation reported sales declined 5% while organic sales grew 4%; segment margin expanded 90 bps to 17.2%.
risks: Post-spin aggregate improvement is uneven by segment; Process Automation and Technology showed organic contraction and margin pressure.
Comparisons must use the disclosed Honeywell Technologies perimeter rather than legacy consolidated Honeywell to avoid false continuity across the Aerospace separation.
contradictions: Building Automation and cash conversion strengthened materially while Process Automation and Technology weakened, so a single undifferentiated post-spin momentum narrative would overstate uniformity.
unknowns: Durability of Building Automation order growth and the timing of Process Automation and Technology margin recovery.
Incremental revenue and margin contribution specifically attributable to autonomous-control products is not isolated in the Q2 release.

recommendation: Use the SEC-filed post-spin perimeter table as the clean operating baseline for Alpha. Preserve segment dispersion and avoid mixing legacy Aerospace economics into current HON calibration.
